title: devbin infra: apply, the Fly runtime leg, dmarc check, and the known-sender library

wps.title: infra apply: Fly end-to-end, DNS and Workspace emit an ordered record list
infra mail dmarc check: the assertion leg, red on a silently missing domain
Fly runtime leg of check: certs, address agreement, release_command, staged secrets

criteria.text: Fly is driven end to end via flyctl, while DNS and Workspace emit an ordered, copy-pasteable record list rather than pretending to apply.
apply exits NON-ZERO when it hands work back. A partial apply reporting success reads as done, and the operator stops.

The legs are ASYMMETRIC and the output must not pretend otherwise. Hover has no public API and no credentials exist in any tree, so a uniform plan-apply-verify would overpromise on the leg that carries the estate.

check owns the ASSERTION and goes RED on a domain that published rua and is silently missing from the reports. That comparison needs a profile, which is why it cannot live in report -- a boundary drawn by what a component CAN know outlasts one drawn by what it should do.

The library ships pair-SHAPE and required-record-CLASS invariants, never values. A shipped value commits to an answer nobody has: a vendor include would have been wrong for a live domain on 2026-09-06, and whether that split is account-specific or generational is unresolved.
Every invariant is profile-overridable, so a project whose vendor differs does not have to fork the library.
The runtime leg checks certificates, A and AAAA agreement, release_command path validity, and staged-secret detection.
